idiom_name: Arc<T> (atomically reference counted) + Arc::make_mut for clone-on-write; Cow<'a, B> for the borrowed sibling
implementation_notes: Rust's standard library contains exactly the classic structure: Arc<T> is 'a thread-safe reference-counting pointer' whose 'atomic operations for its reference counting' make sharing across threads safe, and Arc::make_mut is the copy-on-write step - the docs list it as the clone-on-write way to mutate through an Arc, which 'clones the data only when needed (when there are multiple references)'. A published snapshot is an Arc<T> behind a mutex or a swappable cell; readers clone the Arc (one atomic increment) and hold the value for the whole read. Cow<'a, B> is the same idea with borrows instead of counts ('clone the data lazily when mutation or ownership is required') and is the right type for single-threaded borrow-or-own data, not for cross-thread sharing. Nothing needs hand-writing, and hand-rolling a count would be unsafe: Rc is not Sync and Arc's counter is private.
pitfalls: Arc::make_mut clones the whole body when the count is greater than one: if a reader still holds the snapshot (or a stale Arc lingers in a channel, registry or task), every write pays a full clone - and Arc cycles keep both the body and its count alive forever, so back-edges must be Weak.

The count is atomic, the pointer is not: swapping an Arc<T> field without synchronisation is a data race even though the count itself is safe - publish through a Mutex/RwLock, an atomic pointer cell (arc-swap or a carefully reclamation-managed AtomicPtr), or exclusive access before Arc::make_mut.

Cow is not a shared handle: to_mut clones borrowed data eagerly once ownership is needed, and a Cow that outlives its borrow becomes an owned copy - do not read clone-on-borrow as cross-thread copy-on-write.
sources: The Rust Standard Library, std::sync::Arc - thread safety (atomic reference counting), Arc::make_mut clone-on-write semantics, and the Mutex/RwLock/atomic alternatives for mutation: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Arc.html

The Rust Standard Library, std::borrow::Cow - 'A clone-on-write smart pointer ... clone the data lazily when mutation or ownership is required', with pointers to Rc::make_mut and Arc::make_mut: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/borrow/enum.Cow.html
